lead: A piece of Africa in Valencia. More than 6,000 animals of 150 species in 100,000 m² of African habitats where the barriers are practically invisible.

BIOPARC Valencia is a new-generation zoo located in the Parque de Cabecera, on the banks of the old Turia riverbed. Unlike traditional zoos, at BIOPARC the animals roam freely through spaces that faithfully recreate their natural African habitats, and visitors feel part of those same ecosystems thanks to practically invisible barriers.

Founded in 2008 and with 18 years of history, BIOPARC Valencia is internationally recognised for its model of conservation and animal welfare. The BIOPARC Foundation funds conservation projects on the African continent with part of the park’s income.

items.title: African savanna
items.subtitle: The quintessential African landscape
items.body: BIOPARC’s largest habitat recreates the sub-Saharan savanna with astonishing fidelity. Practically invisible barriers let you share the visual space with the animals, creating the illusion of being in the heart of the African continent. It is home to the park’s most emblematic and largest species.
facts: The queen herd of the savanna, with calves born in the park
BIOPARC was the first zoo in Spain to achieve their breeding in captivity
The king of the savanna in a facility that recreates its natural habitat
They live in the same space alongside impalas and ostriches

items.title: Equatorial Africa
items.subtitle: The jungle where primates are kings
items.body: The dense vegetation of the African equatorial rainforest is home to the great apes and some of the most surprising and hard-to-see species in the wild. The recreation of the ecosystem includes real tropical plants, streams and shaded areas that imitate the true conditions of the central African jungle.
facts: One of the most endangered species on the planet, living as a family
The most intelligent primates, with fascinating social behaviour
Africa’s most elusive cats, usually hard to spot
Forest species that share the undergrowth of the habitat

items.title: African wetlands
items.subtitle: The waters where hippos and crocodiles lie in wait
items.body: Inspired by Kitum Cave in Kenya and by Africa’s great wetland systems, this habitat recreates the shores and inland waters of the continent. A unique experience that lets you watch hippos both from the surface and underwater, through submerged glass panels.
facts: Visible swimming underwater through the glass panels
Africa’s most feared reptile in its recreated natural environment
Colonies of pink flamingos in the habitat’s lagoons
Various species of African birds tied to water and wetlands

items.title: Madagascar Island
items.subtitle: The kingdom of lemurs on Africa’s most singular island
items.body: Madagascar is one of the most biodiverse islands on the planet: 90% of its species exist nowhere else on Earth. BIOPARC recreates this unique ecosystem with up to seven species of lemur, some of them critically endangered, in a space designed to make it easy to get close to and observe these very peculiar primates.
facts: The most recognisable lemur, active and social, in the park
The smallest primates in the world, nocturnal in habit
The largest lemur, known for its calls that echo through the forest
Madagascar’s largest predator, resembling a cat

items.title: The Final Frontier
items.body: An immersive virtual reality experience that takes you to the bottom of the ocean to discover fascinating marine fauna. Available inside the park with advance booking.

items.title: Madagascar tours
items.body: Exclusive guided tours of Madagascar Island to get close to the lemurs and learn about their conservation story with the park’s keepers.

items.title: Meet the keepers
items.body: Join the animal care team during their working day and find out first-hand how they work with animals in a conservation park of this kind.

items.title: Educational workshops
items.body: From preparing bat boxes to animal biology workshops for schoolchildren and families. Check the full programme on the BIOPARC website.

blocks.title: Tips for visiting BIOPARC Valencia
items: Book your ticket online in advance to avoid queues, especially at weekends
Allow at least 3 hours to see all the habitats at a relaxed pace
The animals are most active first thing in the morning and in the late afternoon
The park’s own car park costs €7/day with no need to book in advance
The park is open 365 days a year, including public holidays
